profile.reading: This is Atman Data Center Warsaw-1, at ul. Grochowska 21A in the Praga-Poludnie district of Warsaw, Poland, part of what Atman describes as Polands largest telecom and data center campus, spanning 8 operational buildings with about 12,428 square meters, or roughly 134,000 square feet, of gross data center floor space, plus room to add up to 5 more server buildings for a further 7,000 square meters. The campus carries a total energy allocation of about 57 megawatts, backed by 29,460 kVA of UPS capacity and 16 diesel generators totaling 23,800 kVA, supports power densities up to 10 kilowatts per rack, and rated raised floor loads up to 1,500 kilograms per square meter. The newest building on the campus, designated F6, was commissioned in 2021 with about 1,440 square meters and a guaranteed 3.6 megawatts of IT power. The site holds DCOS-4 certification, the highest level under the Data Centre Operations Standard issued by EPI, and Atman reports the campus runs on 100 percent renewable electricity. Atman itself was founded in 1993 as Polands first commercial internet service provider, launched Polands first inter operator internet exchange point in 1997, an ancestor of todays Atman-IX and THINX exchange ecosystem, began offering colocation services in 2002, and started dedicated data center operations, the basis for this campus, in 2008. The company today describes itself as the largest data center operator in the region after more than 30 years in business, holding ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certification. Atman also operates the Atman-IX internet exchange point at this same Grochowska campus, tracing back to that first 1997 exchange launch, making Warsaw-1 not just a colocation facility but a core interconnection point for Polish and regional internet traffic, a combination of colocation and exchange infrastructure that has helped the company market the site as central to Polands internet backbone rather than simply one data hall among many in the Warsaw market.
